messages.text: Handed to the team · Need JD to confirm the factory Normal Mode preset hashrate and the voltage/frequ

Hi Jack,

You are right on the overclock point and I should have said it that way myself. The Thor's own Overclock preset sits at 730 MHz, so your 500 MHz custom run is still below the factory's own high setting, not an overclock. Thanks for the correction.

Both screenshots came through. On the Dash I can see 6.05 TH/s live with a 6.05 average, efficiency 10.5 J/TH, 4443 shares with 1 rejected for 99.98 percent accepted, Ethernet link up, best difficulty 3.02G, uptime 14 hours 1 minute. On the power panel, 63.7 W draw, 12 V input, ASIC frequency 455 MHz, HB1 voltage 2.02 V, hashboard 1 at 40.9 C in the Safe band. That is a 14 hour sample, so the numbers are real and not a warm up artefact, and your DATUM gateway agreeing with the miner tells us the miner is not inflating or hiding anything.

Here is what those figures actually say about the chip. At 455 MHz you are getting 6.05 TH/s, which is about 13.3 GH/s for every MHz of clock. Apply that same ratio to the 730 MHz overclock preset and you land at roughly 9.7 TH/s, which is essentially the 10 TH/s the unit is rated at in that mode. In other words your silicon is delivering the hashrate its clock allows, and the clock is the thing holding the number down, not a weak or damaged chip. The 63.7 W backs that up: you are drawing below the Normal mode power band we quoted, and 63.7 W divided by 6.05 TH/s is 10.5 J/TH, which is the efficiency the unit is meant to run at. A failing hashboard burns the power and loses the hashrate. Yours is doing neither. Add 40.9 C with automatic fan control on, 99.98 percent accepted shares and a 3.02G best difficulty, and there is no sign of throttling, instability or a sick chip anywhere in that data.

So on your direct question, whether the unit is underperforming: against the clock it is running at, no. What I am less sure of is the 6.6 to 6.8 TH/s I quoted you for Normal Mode, because that band does not fit the 455 MHz the preset actually uses. Either the official Normal figure is nearer 6.2, or the Normal preset is meant to load a slightly higher clock than 455 MHz on your firmware. I do not want to guess between those two, so I have put it to JD, our hardware lead, with your exact readings and screenshots. He picks it up tomorrow from 10am ET and the answer comes to you here in this thread.

If you want it faster, JD is very active on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf as @nullhashrate, and the Thor owners there will recognise your numbers straight away.

In the meantime, nothing is wrong with leaving it on Normal, and if you do want the full 10 TH/s the Overclock preset at 730 MHz is the supported way to get it, with more heat and roughly 155 to 166 W at the wall.

Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
